I am here in Iringa, my maize plot is small, just over half a hectare, and I plant it same way my father showed me. I have no cash for those bags of urea from the dukani — one bag costs too much for what I earn, and last season the rain was good so I will do like last year. I keep some goats and chickens behind the house, so I carry that manure to the plot before the rains, and I save seed from my best cobs like always. I intercrop beans with the maize so the soil stays strong, and my wife and I do the weeding ourselves; only at harvest I sometimes call my brother's son to help carry.
